links.outcome: LLM accuracy on clinician-generated EHR questions by reasoning hop count
links.effect: Accuracy declined monotonically with hop count across all three models: Claude Sonnet 30.6% to 17.6%, GPT-4o 37.8% to 14.7%, GPT-5.4 37.8% to 23.5%.
links.quote: All three models, spanning two providers and two OpenAI generations (GPT-4 and GPT-5), show monotone accuracy decline with hop count: Claude Sonnet zero-shot falls from 30.6% (hop=1) to 17.6% (hop=4) (Cochran-Armitage z=-2.30, p=0.011; OR per hop 0.72, 95% CI [0.56,0.92], p=0.008); GPT-4o replicates this (37.8% to 14.7%; OR 0.58 [0.45,0.75], p<0.001); and gpt-5.4-2026-03-05 confirms it (37.8% to 23.5%; OR 0.80 [0.66,0.98], p=0.027).

unlisted_practices: Stratifying deployment risk of clinical LLMs by compositional reasoning depth (hop count) of the task
Extended thinking/reasoning mode to mitigate multi-step reasoning errors (did not significantly flatten accuracy-depth curve)

screen.reason: Evaluates LLM performance across reasoning depth/hop count on an EHR question answering benchmark dataset (MedAlign) without testing an organizational deployment practice or guardrail.
